statement: `topic()` takes an optional `derive:` plan, built with `@isoloop/derive`'s builder, that names its source topics. The derived topic's schema checks the plan's output like any topic's.

events.why: Every app that wants a windowed sum or a filtered stream writes the same headless isolate again.

statement: A plan is a serialisable tree of operators, not code. v1's operators are filter, map, window, groupBy and aggregate.

events.why: A spec can carry a plan, and a small operator set is easier to check, explain and run in two engines than a query language.

statement: Each derived topic is kept by one derive isolate: a headless isolate the kernel spawns and owns, running a fixed engine and no user code. Derivations never run in the bus worker.

events.why: Every topic depends on the bus worker, so a heavy derivation there would stall them all.

statement: A light derive isolate shares a `derive` pool and a heavy one gets its own worker, set per topic.

events.why: Derive isolates cost a worker each unless they share; the kernel picking a pool goes against ADR 0001 and is still to grill.

statement: A blocked or crashed derive isolate is restarted by the supervisor and resumes from its committed offset on each source, while the bus and other topics keep running.

events.why: A blocked derivation stalls only its own topic.

statement: Subscribing to or watching a derived topic needs the subscribe grant on it and on every one of its sources, checked at subscribe time.

events.why: A derived topic must not be a way to read what the reader couldn't read itself.

statement: The derive isolate runs a plan through one engine interface. A TypeScript reference engine ships first, with an engine conformance suite.

events.why: Two engines must give the same results, and the TypeScript one needs only the bus.

statement: A Rust engine compiled to WASM runs behind the same interface, and ships only if it does better than the TypeScript engine on the M13 benchmark gate.

events.why: Columnar work with SIMD and threads can beat per-record JavaScript, but only when data and work stay in the engine.

statement: Devtools shows a row per derived topic, with its plan, its lag behind each source and its engine, and lists derive isolates as the kernel's.

events.why: A developer needs to see why a derived topic is behind.
